implementation_notes: Default TypeScript realization where Kafka is the broker: the group id is the durable subscription identity, and eachBatch puts the commit point in the handler's hands. Choose it when the service already runs on Kafka and catch-up must be bounded explicitly rather than left to the library's polling loop.
pitfalls: Resolved-but-uncommitted offsets are replayed after a crash; the handler must tolerate that.
Disabling autoResolve without calling resolveOffset stalls commit progress and lets the backlog grow unboundedly.

variants.name: MQTT persistent session with mqtt.js (clean:false)
variants.idiom_name: mqtt.connect({clientId, clean:false}) with a typed message handler
variants.implementation_notes: Where MQTT is the transport, the broker keeps the session for the clientId and queues QoS 1/2 publications while the client is offline. Choose it for browser-adjacent or edge Node consumers where per-client sessions are the natural unit of retention.
pitfalls: Re-subscribing on every connect is safe but not sufficient: without a stable client id and session expiry there is nothing to resume.
QoS 1 means duplicates are normal; deduplicate on the application message id.
